title: 4 NEW MSFS Activity Packs! airBaltic A220, MD-11 Master Bundle & Extreme Alps Landings
description:
Ready to master structured commercial airline rotations and test your mountain approach skills in Microsoft Flight Simulator 2020? The Marketplace just expanded with four brand-new activity releases from Perfect Flight—featuring scheduled European airline operations with airBaltic and PLAY, high-intensity Alpine landing drills, and a dedicated multi-livery master collection for the legendary MD-11!

In this structured marketplace breakdown, we cut through the storefront clutter and organize these arrivals into logical categories with key aircraft compatibility notes and prerequisite warnings to help you plan your next flight session:

✈️ SCHEDULED EUROPEAN COMMERCIAL ROTATIONS (A220 & A320neo)
Step into scheduled line operations with fully briefed airline activity packs:

airBaltic A220 Fall 2026 (12 Legs): Fly 12 comprehensive IFR scheduled rotations across Europe complete with custom voice briefings and simulated in-flight events. (Important prerequisite: Requires the Synaptic A220 with livery pack or the Virtualcol A220 series).

PLAY Europe Charter (8 Legs): Command eight VIP and charter rotations transporting sports teams, symphony orchestras, and film crews across European destinations including London, Munich, Dubrovnik, Naples, and Geneva. Features the custom PLAY livery configured specifically for the default Asobo A320neo V1.

🏔️ HEAVY IRON MASTER BUNDLES & ALPINE CHALLENGES
From classic tri-jet line flying to extreme short-field mountain arrivals:

MD-11 Master Collection: A discounted all-in-one bundle bringing together previously released Advanced and Adventure packs for the TFDi Design MD-11. Includes 4 operational packages featuring American Airlines, Delta Air Lines, KLM, and LTU International routes at a combined discount.

Advanced Challenges: Alps Landings (24 Scenarios): Put your stick-and-rudder precision to the test across 24 mostly handcrafted alpine landing scenarios in France, Switzerland, Italy, and Austria. Tackle steep altiport approaches like Courchevel (LFLJ) with its 18.6% gradient, navigate high-altitude mountain passes above 7,000 feet, and grease the centerline on complex valley arrivals into Innsbruck and Sion across STOL bush planes, turboprops, business jets, and twin-engine airliners.

Whether you're working through scheduled regional turns in the A220, cruising with classic tri-jet power in the MD-11, or executing cross-slope landings in the Alps, these additions bring rewarding operational depth to your simulator.

Which of these activity packs are you loading into your flight computer first? Let us know in the comments below!

If you find these marketplace breakdowns helpful, don't forget to hit the like button, subscribe for weekly flight sim coverage, and clear skies on your next flight!
